intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that multiple epiphyseal dysplasia-2 (EDM2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the COL9A2 gene (120260) on chromosome 1p34.2.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia-2 (EDM2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the COL9A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation screening of candidate regions revealed a novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region.
checks.explanation: The abstract links a COL9A2 mutation to EDM2. It does not say the mutation is heterozygous, although the family's dominant inheritance pattern implies it.

checks.claim: The COL9A2 gene is located on chromosome 1p34.2.
checks.evidence_quote: we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1, in a region containing the gene (COL9A2)
checks.explanation: The abstract places COL9A2 on 1p. The band 1p34.2 is standard locus nomenclature that restates this location, so it counts as supported under the rules.

paragraphs.text: Briggs et al. (1994) described multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) as a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia with mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis. They noted that some forms look clinically like mild pseudoachondroplasia (PSACH). In the EDM2 form, the hips are not markedly affected early in life (Fiedler et al., 2002).

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is characterized by mild short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is characterized by early-onset osteoarthrosis.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis

checks.claim: Some forms of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia look clinically like mild pseudoachondroplasia (PSACH).
checks.evidence_quote: Some forms of MED clinically resemble another chondrodysplasia phenotype, the mild form of pseudoachondroplasia (PSACH).

checks.claim: In multiple epiphyseal dysplasia-2 (EDM2), the hips are not markedly affected early in life.
checks.evidence_quote: a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) in which the hips are not markedly affected at early age (EDM2)

paragraphs.text: Versteylen et al. (1988) described 2 families that appeared to have multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. Severe osteochondritis dissecans of the knees was strikingly common in both families. The authors suggested that the osteochondritis was caused by the fragmented, maldeveloped epiphyses typical of epiphyseal dysplasia.

checks.claim: Versteylen et al. (1988) described 2 families that appeared to have multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Two families are described which appear to contain examples of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states that 2 families appeared to have multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.

checks.claim: Severe osteochondritis dissecans of the knees was strikingly common in both families described by Versteylen et al. (1988).
checks.evidence_quote: In both families a striking incidence of severe osteochondritis of the knees was encountered.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a striking incidence of severe knee osteochondritis in both families. The title specifies that this is osteochondritis dissecans.

checks.claim: Versteylen et al. (1988) suggested that the osteochondritis dissecans in these families was caused by the fragmented, maldeveloped epiphyses typical of epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: It is suggested that this was caused by the fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses characteristic of epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this causal suggestion directly.

paragraphs.text: Fiedler et al. (2002) described a 4-generation family of 19 individuals, 12 of whom had a variant of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. From childhood, the disease caused pain and stiffness in the knees, ankles, elbows, and finger joints. Some adults had repeated free articular bodies that locked the joint, and affected individuals tended to develop early degenerative joint disease. The hips were not markedly affected at an early age.

checks.claim: Fiedler et al. (2002) described a 4-generation family of 19 individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a family of 19 individuals over four generations

checks.claim: In the 4-generation family described by Fiedler et al. (2002), 12 of 19 individuals had a variant of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a family of 19 individuals over four generations in which 12 members are affected with a variant of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.

checks.claim: In the family described by Fiedler et al. (2002), multiple epiphyseal dysplasia caused pain and stiffness in the knees, ankles, elbows, and finger joints from childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Beginning in childhood, the disease leads to pain and stiffness of knees, ankles, elbows and finger joints.

checks.claim: Some affected adults in the family described by Fiedler et al. (2002) had repeated free articular bodies that locked the joint.
checks.evidence_quote: Some adult patients repeatedly suffer from free articular bodies resulting in locking of the joint.

checks.claim: Affected individuals in the family described by Fiedler et al. (2002) tended to develop early degenerative joint disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Finally, affected individuals are prone to the development of early degenerative joint disease.

checks.claim: In the family described by Fiedler et al. (2002), the hips were not markedly affected at an early age.
checks.evidence_quote: a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) in which the hips are not markedly affected at early age (EDM2)
checks.explanation: The abstract describes hip sparing as a feature of the EDM2 subtype (the title says 'relative hip sparing during childhood'). It does not explicitly describe the hips of this family's members.

paragraphs.text: Briggs et al. (1994) described multiple epiphyseal dysplasia as dominantly inherited. In the 4-generation family reported by Fiedler et al. (2002), the COL9A2 mutation was found in affected members.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) described multiple epiphyseal dysplasia as dominantly inherited.
checks.evidence_quote: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia

checks.claim: In the 4-generation family reported by Fiedler et al. (2002), the COL9A2 mutation was found in affected members.
checks.evidence_quote: We confirmed the nucleotide substitution in eight clinically affected family members as well as in three presymptomatic young children.

paragraphs.text: Briggs et al. (1994) studied a large family with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. Linkage studies with chromosome 19 markers excluded the interval previously linked to PSACH and to one form of MED. Using this family, they identified an MED locus, EDM2, on the short arm of chromosome 1. The region contains COL9A2, which encodes the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen, a structural component of the cartilage extracellular matrix.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) studied a large family with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED

checks.claim: In the large MED family studied by Briggs et al. (1994), linkage studies with chromosome 19 markers excluded the interval previously linked to PSACH and to one form of MED.
checks.evidence_quote: both mild and severe PSACH as well as a form of MED have been linked to the same interval on chromosome 19 ... Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the family excluded the chromosome 19 interval that had been linked to PSACH and to one form of MED.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) identified an MED locus, EDM2, on the short arm of chromosome 1 using a large MED family.
checks.evidence_quote: Using this family, we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1
checks.explanation: Stated directly; the locus is named EDM2 in the paper's title.

checks.claim: The EDM2 region on chromosome 1p contains the COL9A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: in a region containing the gene (COL9A2) that encodes the alpha 2 chain of type IX collagen

checks.claim: COL9A2 encodes the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen, a structural component of the cartilage extracellular matrix.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene (COL9A2) that encodes the alpha 2 chain of type IX collagen, a structural component of the cartilage extracellular matrix

paragraphs.text: Warman et al. (1994) used fluorescence in situ hybridization to map the COL9A2 gene to human chromosome 1p32.3-p33. Using a single-strand conformational polymorphism in the murine Col9a2 gene, they mapped the mouse gene to chromosome 4.

checks.claim: Warman et al. (1994) used fluorescence in situ hybridization to map the human COL9A2 gene to chromosome 1p32.3-p33.
checks.evidence_quote: COL9A2 was mapped to human chromosome 1p32.3-p33 using fluorescence in situ hybridization.

checks.claim: Warman et al. (1994) used a single-strand conformational polymorphism in the murine Col9a2 gene to map the mouse Col9a2 gene to chromosome 4.
checks.evidence_quote: A single-strand conformational polymorphism within the murine Col9a2 gene was used to map this locus to mouse chromosome 4.

paragraphs.text: Briggs et al. (1994) excluded the chromosome 19 interval in a large MED family that mapped instead to chromosome 1p. That interval had previously been linked to mild and severe PSACH and to one form of MED. The finding showed that multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) excluded the chromosome 19 interval in a large MED family that mapped instead to chromosome 1p.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval. Using this family, we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1

checks.claim: The chromosome 19 interval excluded by Briggs et al. (1994) had previously been linked to mild and severe PSACH and to one form of MED.
checks.evidence_quote: Recently, both mild and severe PSACH as well as a form of MED have been linked to the same interval on chromosome 19

checks.claim: The finding by Briggs et al. (1994) showed that multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: a form of MED have been linked to the same interval on chromosome 19 ... we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1
checks.explanation: The abstract does not use the word 'heterogeneous'. However, it shows that one form of MED maps to chromosome 19 and another to chromosome 1p, so genetic heterogeneity follows directly.

paragraphs.text: Muragaki et al. (1996) reported that a mutation in the COL9A2 gene, which encodes the alpha-2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).

checks.claim: COL9A2 encodes the alpha-2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX.
checks.evidence_quote: A mutation in the gene encoding the alpha 2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, COL9A2

checks.claim: Muragaki et al. (1996) reported that a mutation in the COL9A2 gene causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).
checks.evidence_quote: A mutation in the gene encoding the alpha 2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, COL9A2, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).

paragraphs.text: In the 4-generation family with EDM2 reported by Fiedler et al. (2002), screening of candidate regions identified a new G-to-C change at position -1 of the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splice region. The authors thought this change most likely alters splicing. Sequencing and BsaWI digestion confirmed the change in 8 clinically affected family members and in 3 young children who did not yet have symptoms.

checks.claim: In the 4-generation EDM2 family reported by Fiedler et al. (2002), screening of candidate regions identified a new G-to-C change at position -1 of the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splice region.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation screening of candidate regions revealed a novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region. This G --> C substitution

checks.claim: Fiedler et al. (2002) thought the G-to-C change at position -1 of the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splice region most likely alters splicing.
checks.evidence_quote: This G --> C substitution most probably induces an alteration of the splicing process.

checks.claim: Sequencing and BsaWI digestion confirmed the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 G-to-C change in 8 clinically affected members of the family reported by Fiedler et al. (2002).
checks.evidence_quote: Family screening was carried out by both automated sequencing and by digestion of amplicons with BsaWI. We confirmed the nucleotide substitution in eight clinically affected family members

checks.claim: The COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 G-to-C change was also found in 3 young children who did not yet have symptoms in the family reported by Fiedler et al. (2002).
checks.evidence_quote: We confirmed the nucleotide substitution in eight clinically affected family members as well as in three presymptomatic young children.

paragraphs.text: Fiedler et al. (2002) examined free articular bodies, removed by arthroscopy from 2 patients, by electron microscopy. Collagen fibril diameter did not differ obviously from that of normal articular cartilage. Taking previous reports into account, they suggested that mutations causing skipping of COL9A2 exon 3, in the COL3 domain of the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen, may be fairly common in the MED subtype in which the hips are not markedly affected early in life (EDM2).

checks.claim: Fiedler et al. (2002) used electron microscopy to examine free articular bodies removed by arthroscopy from 2 patients with EDM2.
checks.evidence_quote: Electron microscopy showed that the diameter of collagen fibrils from arthroscopically removed free articular bodies of two patients
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract; the two patients come from the EDM2 family.

checks.claim: In the free articular bodies from 2 EDM2 patients examined by Fiedler et al. (2002), collagen fibril diameter did not differ obviously from that of normal articular cartilage.
checks.evidence_quote: the diameter of collagen fibrils from arthroscopically removed free articular bodies of two patients was not obviously different from that of normal articular cartilage

checks.claim: Fiedler et al. (2002) suggested that mutations causing skipping of COL9A2 exon 3, in the COL3 domain of the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen, may be fairly common in the MED subtype in which the hips are not markedly affected early in life (EDM2).
checks.evidence_quote: mutations leading to skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha2-chain of collagen type IX may be relatively common in patients with a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) in which the hips are not markedly affected at early age (EDM2)

paragraphs.text: Nakashima et al. (2005) reported that double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation. This radiographic sign alone therefore does not indicate the DTDST-related form of MED.

checks.claim: Nakashima et al. (2005) reported that double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation.
checks.explanation: The claim restates the paper's title almost word for word.

checks.claim: Double-layered patella alone does not indicate the DTDST-related form of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation.
checks.explanation: This is an inference, but a direct one: if the sign also occurs in MED without DTDST mutation, it cannot by itself indicate the DTDST-related form. Only the title was available.

paragraphs.text: Fiedler et al. (2002) studied a 4-generation family with EDM2 in which the hips were not markedly affected at an early age. In this family they identified a G-to-C change at position -1 of the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splice region, which they thought most likely alters splicing. Sequencing and BsaWI digestion confirmed the change in 8 clinically affected family members and in 3 young children who did not yet have symptoms.
